title: Can ChatGPT or Claude make you money if you let it trade your crypto account?
author: RobodOfficial
selftext:
“Connect your exchange account and let AI handle the trades.”  
Before connecting anything, ask the provider to walk you through one trade from the strategy. What triggered the entry? How big was the position? What made it exit?  
Giving a bot trading access is like handing someone your car keys. They can start the car. You still need to agree on where they’re going and what to do when the road is blocked.  
A bot can use ChatGPT or Claude to help analyze an idea. If the software also has permission to place orders, it can act on its rules with your money. That’s when details like position size and when to stop start to matter.  
One example helps you understand the rules. Then ask to see how those same rules performed across a series of trades, including the losing ones. How much was left after fees? How far did the account fall during its worst stretch?  
If the pitch promises a fixed daily return or asks you to send your API secret in a DM, take that as a reason to walk away.  
At Robod, we build tools for the research step. We’d start with a rule we can explain and a historical test we can inspect before giving any bot permission to trade.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body: This article is pretty unclear — mostly a jumble of words. ChatGPT or Claude agents will not, at least for now, be able to trade profitably on their own. If you want to lose your money quickly and spectacularly, by all means connect an agent and watch it trade. Agents are tools that help you build and refine your own strategy. An agent won’t invent a trading strategy for you or hand you alpha. That’s a myth.

comments.author: mrgizmo212
comments.body:
NO, ChatGPT or Claude cannot make you money consistently if you give it access to your crypto account. 

Can it get lucky and hit a trade or 2 MAYBE. What’s more likely to happen is:  
\- delayed executions   
\- open orders that are forgotten and or mismanaged  
\- over sizing your risk  
\- hallucinations that don’t just cause frustration but actual money lol. 

There’s a lot more to list but you get the idea.  

Can it be used as a copilot or tool for strategy or research? Of course! But it’s not your get rich on autopilot secret and anyone claiming that is full of shit.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good checklist, and the walk-through of one trade is a great test of whether someone really understands their own bot. One thing I'd add is to use API keys that can only trade and can't withdraw, so the worst case is a bad trade, not an empty account. I'd also run any new bot in paper mode first and compare it to what it claims. Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent lets you run an AI agent on a practice balance, and its Exchange Connections use trade-only keys on your own exchange.
